paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of WMoCu alloy doped with different sized Mo particles
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: WMoCu alloys doped with Mo particles in the nanoscale or microscale range were prepared by infiltration process using the element Ni as an activating element.
The tensile strengths of WMoCu(M), WMoCu(N) alloy, and WCu alloy are 381 MPa, 321 MPa, and 242 MPa, respectively.

Firstly, the W powder, Mo powder and Ni powder were mixed in a home-made powder mixer according to the composition in Table 1 and milled for 6 h at 60 rpm with the ball-to-powder ratio of 5:1.

Secondly, the mixed powders were pressed into the W–Mo skeletons using a four-column hydraulic press at a pressure of 210 MPa for 1 min. The W–Mo skeleton had a size of 40 mm in diameter and 11 mm in length.
Thirdly, the prepared W–Mo skeleton was pre-sintered at 900 °C for 1.5 h in the hydrogen atmosphere.

evidence.section: 3.2 Formation process and microstructure of WMo skeleton
evidence.quote: During the cooling process, partially dissolved W and Mo atoms in the CuNi(L) alloy liquid phase preferentially recrystallize around Mo or W particles to form WMo solid solution and form a core-shell structure.

The dissolution of solute atoms distorts the solid solution lattice which, consequently, hinders the distortion sliding and makes the sliding deformation of the metal more difficult, thereby increasing the strength of the alloy
